title: How Macy's Thanksgiving Parade Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade: its origins as the 1924-era Macy's Christmas Parade staffed by immigrant employees, the shift from caged animals to balloons and floats, Tony Sarg and Gene McFadden's influence, how giant character balloons are designed and inflated (including Inflation Day and the Museum of Natural History), handler requirements, notable mishaps like the Cat in the Hat and Barney balloon incidents and the 2005 Eminem balloon accident, float construction and costumes, celebrity appearances and lip-syncing controversies, sponsorship costs, viewing tips, and how the 2020 pandemic parade was TV-only. Ends with a listener mail segment on Australian compulsory voting.
topics: Cat in the Hat balloon accident

segments.title: Opening banter and parade fandom
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the episode and talk about watching the parade, Inflation Day, and a friend who has marched in the parade.

segments.title: Origins as the Macy's Christmas Parade
segments.summary: The parade began as the Macy's Christmas Parade, run by immigrant employees, with about a quarter million attendees in the first year along a six-mile route from Harlem to Herald Square. Caged animals were replaced by floats in the 1927 era, and the parade became a Thanksgiving event by the mid-1930s; celebrities began appearing around 1934, with Eddie Cantor noted as an early one.

segments.title: Balloons, Tony Sarg, and early promotions
segments.summary: Tony Sarg, a puppeteer and designer, created the first floats and balloons and staged a sea monster prank on Nantucket. Macy's ran a balloon-return promotion for four years, ended after airplanes chased the balloons. Discussion of the Flagship store's wooden escalators.

segments.title: How giant balloons are designed and built
segments.summary: Balloons start as hand-drawn sketches, move to 3D modeling and 3D-printed versions, and are built in chambers so a limb or leg failure does not bring the whole balloon down. Most are about five or six stories tall. Production moved from a Tootsie Roll factory in Hoboken to a larger studio in New Jersey.

segments.title: Balloon artists, Keith Haring, and helium
segments.summary: Celebrity artist balloons in the Blue Sky Gallery series, including Yayoi Kusama, Takashi Murakami and a Keith Haring balloon that flew in 2008 as a tribute to the late artist. Discussion of the parade's helium use, roughly 400,000 cubic feet a year, and the helium supply.

segments.title: Inflation Day, handlers, and balloon mishaps
segments.summary: Balloons are inflated and netted the night before, then handled by up to around 3,000 Macy's employees and friends and family. Handlers need training and health checks, and an NYPD officer trained in balloon handling marches along. Notable accidents include a Sonic the Hedgehog balloon knocking a street lamp onto an off-duty police captain, a Cat in the Hat balloon injuring a woman in 1997, a 2005 Eminem balloon incident injuring two sisters, and the 2008 Keith Haring balloon sideswiping the NBC broadcast (the broadcast was not actually knocked off the air). Wind rules and street light removal followed.
topics: Cat in the Hat balloon accident

segments.title: Floats, costumes, and hosts
segments.summary: Floats are built from welded metal and collapsible designs, introduced by Manford Bass so they could pass through the Lincoln Tunnel. Costume house holds around 5,000 costumes; Tony Sarg is cited as an early host, later replaced by celebrity hosts including Jackie Gleason and Andy Kaufman appearances.

segments.title: Sponsorships, costs, and celebrity performances
segments.summary: The parade began selling sponsorships, a change pushed by Gene McFadden in the late 1970s. Estimated costs and sponsor fees are discussed as unconfirmed. The Miami Vice float, Kiss on a Ocean Spray float, John Legend's lip-syncing apology, and Melba Moore's lip-sync are covered.

segments.title: Munsters float and 1994 parade drunken incident
segments.summary: Fred Gwynn and Al Lewis reprised the Munsters for a float in 1994; Gwynn reportedly drank heavily on board and shouted at the hosts, and the music was turned up to drown him out.
topics: parade hosts Betty White and Lauren Chapin

segments.title: Viewing tips and the 2020 TV-only parade
segments.summary: Viewing tips include arriving early on Central Park West, bringing a plastic bag as a raincoat or seat, and the fact that seats at the end are reserved. The 2020 parade was held as a TV-only event in front of Herald Square with social distancing and masks.

segments.title: Listener mail: Australian compulsory voting
segments.summary: A listener named Jackie writes that Australia's compulsory voting works well, with weekend voting and sausage sizzles, and that the US system seems odd by comparison.
